Whereupon, not long ago, I learned from a man worthy of belief that, shortly before I wrote these things, there was separated, by judgment of the Official of Albi [the bishop's judge], the marriage of a husband who had remained eighteen years without ever having been able to approach his wife, who, being examined, was found still a virgin; and nevertheless she had never made any show of being vexed or complaining of it.

At the end of the said nine years she was unbewitched, and to this end instructed to have four masses said, which she did; and she names the priests, and says that one of them (whom she set down by name) made her eat some hosts and fouaces [hearth cakes], from which she and her said husband found themselves so well that she conceived, immediately afterwards, a son, still living, called Sanxi Guerre.

Incredible certainly is the ruse and wiliness of Satan, who, like a roaring lion, ever walks about around men, to catch and deceive some one of them, a transfiguring himself oftentimes into an Angel of light, the better to envelop and entice him b; nay, he so well embellishes and adorns his darkness with his colours that to many the very night and obscurity seem to be a splendour and perfect light — as in this unbewitching, in which, under the pretext of piety and of ecclesiastical ceremonies, he grafted a horrible and cruel poison, persuading these poor married people that there was no other means to unbewitch than the superstition of eating hosts and fouaces, thus leaving aside contrition of heart, humiliation of spirit, alms, fasts and prayers, which are the true and excellent exorcisms to present to God c, placing in Him all one's hope, and not in
